title: Start Lead Work from Email Using an Action Chip
description: Convert a new lead email into a unified operational workflow without creating siloed records by starting with an Action Chip.
prerequisites: You can access Email Hub, Contacts, and Tasks modules.
The inbound lead email is visible in Email Hub.
You have permission to create Action Chips and linked records.
steps: Open Email Hub and select the lead email you want to process.
Create an Action Chip directly from that email instead of creating records in separate tools.
Confirm the chip creates or links a Unified Identity in Contact Hub for the lead.
Use the same Action Chip context to generate needed follow-on items such as a quote, time log, or Kanban task.
Keep all updates on the same chip-linked workflow so every operational event stays tethered to the lead identity.
Review the lead timeline and verify the chain of custody links email, contact identity, tasks, and financial outputs.
validations: The lead has one Unified Identity record, not duplicate siloed records.
Generated quote, tasks, or time entries are visibly linked to the originating Action Chip.
Audit trail shows source email through to downstream operational actions.
commonErrors: A separate CRM/contact record is created outside the Action Chip flow.
Downstream task or quote is created but not linked to the originating lead chip.
Duplicate identities appear for the same lead email.
recovery: Merge duplicate lead identities into a single Unified Identity.
Relink orphaned quote/task/time entries to the source Action Chip.
Restart from Email Hub for future leads so linkage is automatic from step one.

faq.question: Why should I start from Email Hub instead of creating a separate CRM record first?
faq.answer: Starting from Email Hub with an Action Chip preserves a single connected record lineage and avoids siloed data.

faq.question: Can I still create quotes and tasks from this flow?
faq.answer: Yes. You can generate quotes, time logs, and Kanban tasks from the same Action Chip while preserving linkage.
